459	## 8. Known limitations (copy into handoff.md §Deployment / §Known limitations)
460	
461	- **Accept-and-rank**: leaderboard and PvP inputs are self-reported; "server-authoritative" covers the verdict and
462	  roster bookkeeping only. A one-line client edit wins every match. Bounded by rate limit, body cap, cooldown.
463	- Free web service sleeps after 15 min idle; cold start ≈ 1 min exceeds `NET_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) — the first
464	  leaderboard/PvP click after a long idle may fail with `network`; opening the menu warms the dyno; retry works.
465	  750 h/month cap.
466	- Free Postgres expires 30 days after creation (14-day grace), no backups: identities and the board are
467	  disposable; rotation is manual (§7). Expiry date recorded in AGENTS.md §Server / meta.json `db_expires`.
468	- Single instance: in-memory rate limiter resets on restart; steal is two non-transactional row updates.
469	- Defenders learn about a stolen companion only on their next upload (§5 step 7); until then the local roster
470	  keeps a ghost companion that still attacks locally but is absent from the server snapshot.
471	- Background uploads ignore `removed`; the correction arrives on the next menu-driven sync.
472	- Bot matches ("Training Dummy") never steal either way; a player alone on the board can only fight the bot.
473	- Probe accounts (`probe-*`, bestIndex 0) accumulate at the bottom of the board, one per network AC run.
474	- No nickname uniqueness, no moderation, no token rotation, no CORS (Electron main is the only client).

# SPEC — Desktop Monster (DesMon)
<!-- RULES: no TBDs. Every feature row must have an AC a shell can decide.
     Ambiguities become numbered Assumptions with rationale.
     Worker column (F28+ table) = claude | codex by the plan-grammar file-set

     src/renderer/{anim,hud,effects}.ts, static/{style,menu}.css and their
     tests); the Planner may override only toward claude, with a Notes line.
     codex rows get vitest/grep/test -e/node -e ACs only (never smoke).
     No external network or hostnames in a feature AC; loopback 127.0.0.1 is
     allowed only for the server-scaffold boot proof (F43 / T22). The only
     external network check is the ## Deployment AC, guarded by
     DESMON_SKIP_NET=1. Table-cell ACs never contain the `|` character (rows
     are extracted by line and executed literally). -->

## Summary

DesMon is a BongoCat-style macOS desktop companion: a small transparent,
frameless, always-on-top pixel-art overlay in which every keystroke or mouse
click makes a sword-wielding pixel knight attack a monster. Monsters have HP
bars; killed monsters scatter into pixels, drop items that are auto-collected,
grant XP, and are replaced by a stronger monster, while the hero levels up.
v2 (0.2.0) adds: every 8th monster is a boss that can be captured into a
30-companion roster that attacks alongside the hero; fever mode; a companion
lifecycle (consume / fuse / reincarnate / sacrifice / rebirth); unbounded
A–Z-suffixed damage numbers on native `bigint`; a Collection & Battle window;
and a leaderboard + asynchronous PvP with companion stealing against a small
Node server (`src/server`, Render free tier) — offline-first, the game never
waits on the network. Built with Electron + TypeScript, all art and sound
generated from code committed in-repo, verified end-to-end by the frozen
AGENTS.md command contract (`npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`,
`npm run smoke`, `npm run package`, `npm run start:server`).

## Assumptions

1. Hero stands on the LEFT facing right; monster on the RIGHT facing left — the requirement allows either side; fixing one makes rendering and tests deterministic.
2. Attack triggers are every `keydown` (OS auto-repeat included) and every `mousedown`, each counting as exactly one attack; key-up, mouse-up, scroll and mouse-move do not — matches the BongoCat per-event feel and is the simplest countable rule.
3. Progression formulas are frozen to GAME_ARCHITECTURE §2 as amended by GAME_DESIGN_V2 §1: `damageForLevel(l)=l`; crit chance 10% × multiplier 2; `monsterMaxHp(i)=⌊10·115^i/100^i⌋` computed as an exact `bigint` (`(10n*115n**i)/100n**i`, equal to the v1 double `⌊10·1.15^i⌋` for every i < 199); `xpReward(i)=5+3i`; `xpToNext(l)=⌊20·1.4^(l−1)⌋`; coins per kill `1+⌊i/3⌋`; trinket chance 25%; hero damage = `level × (crit ? 2 : 1) × (fever ? 3 : 1) × (1 + souls)` — exact formulas make every AC numerically decidable.
4. Exactly 5 monster species (slime, bat, ghost, golem, dragon) cycle forever, with a palette tint per `tier = ⌊index/5⌋`; every 8th monster (`index % 8 === 7`: 7, 15, 23 …) is a boss with 5× HP, 5× XP, 5× coins, a ` BOSS` name suffix and `MonsterDef.boss = true`, drawn at 3× with a crown — 8 is not a multiple of 5 so bosses cycle all species; bounds art effort while making endless scaling visible.
5. Progression is endless: no win state, no final boss. Rebirth at `monsterIndex ≥ 40` is a soft prestige: `souls += ⌊index/8⌋`, `rebirths + 1`, run resets to level 1 / monster 0 while companions, items, coins, kills, bestIndex and nextCompanionId are kept — DesMon stays a companion toy; souls multiply damage by `(1 + souls)`.
6. Trinket items are collection-only counters (5 kinds, weighted) with zero gameplay effect — keeps the engine minimal; coins and trinkets are just HUD/save counters.
7. The save file is `app.getPath('userData')/save.json` (`app.setName('DesMon')` so dev and packaged share it), schema `SaveFileV2` (bigint fields as decimal strings); `parseSave` migrates v1 saves and junk per field (independent fallbacks to `DEFAULT_SAVE`) and never throws — the app must never fail to boot because of a bad save; `serializeSave`/`createEngine` accept `SaveFileV1 | SaveFileV2`.
8. Damage is applied at input time; animations are presentation-only and never gate game logic — keeps the engine deterministic and key-mash-safe.
9. Animation timing state machines (hero IDLE/ATTACK; monster SPAWNING/IDLE/HIT/DYING) are pure functions in `src/core/fsm.ts`, advanced by injected `dt`, consumed by the renderer — the only way animation timing is unit-testable without a DOM.

  `npm run start:server`, health path `/healthz`, build-filter paths
  `src/server/** src/core/** src/shared/** package.json package-lock.json
  tsconfig.main.json .node-version`), Postgres `desmon-db` (internal
  connection string as `DATABASE_URL`). Provisioning is
  `.harness/v2/loop/render-bootstrap.sh` (idempotent by name; `KEY=value`
  output: `SERVER_URL`, `SRV_ID`, `DB_ID`, `DB_CREATED`, `DB_EXPIRES`), run
  only by the loop's deploy task (F50); deploys are explicit
  (`git push origin main` + `render deploys create <srv-id> --wait --confirm`).
- `SERVER_URL=<set by render-bootstrap>` — placeholder until the deploy task
  runs the bootstrap; recorded in AGENTS.md §Server (`SERVER_URL=`,
  `RENDER_SERVICE_ID=`, `RENDER_POSTGRES_ID=`, `DB_CREATED=`, `DB_EXPIRES=`,
  `DEPLOYED_SHA=`), `src/shared/serverUrl.ts`, and
  `.agentdoc/<TS>/meta.json` (`server_url`, `db_expires`).
- Health contract: `GET $SERVER_URL/healthz` → `200 {"ok":true,"sha":"<sha>"}`
  where `<sha>` is an ancestor of `main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD`)
  and no commit after it touches the build-filter paths
  (`git log <sha>..HEAD -- src/server src/core src/shared package.json
  package-lock.json tsconfig.main.json .node-version` is empty). No equality
  check against HEAD — the live sha may legitimately be older. Otherwise
  redeploy (push + `render deploys create --wait`).
- Free-tier facts: the service sleeps after 15 min idle (~60 s cold start,
  longer than `NET_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` — the first leaderboard/PvP click after
  a long idle may report `network`; opening the menu warms the dyno; retry
  works) — the client uses `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, never throws and is
  offline by default; free Postgres expires 30 days after creation
  (`db_expires`, 14-day grace, no backups; identities and the board are
  disposable) — the server runs idempotent DDL on boot so a recreated DB is a
  one-command recovery; clients hit 401 and re-register. Rotation is manual
  (dashboard edit or service recreation under the same name).
- Node pinned by `.node-version` = `20.12.2`. `pg` lives in devDependencies
  (Render installs with `--include=dev`); the .app excludes
  `dist/electron/server/**`.
- Probe: `node dist/electron/server/probe.js "$SERVER_URL"` registers
  `probe-<4hex>`, uploads an empty snapshot and reads the leaderboard
  (`me.rank ≥ 1`); it never plays PvP.

## Input Abstraction (mandatory)

Input & clock abstraction — every source of non-determinism is injected.

- `InputDriver` interface (`src/core/input.ts`): `start()`, `stop()`,
  `subscribe(cb)` → unsubscribe; emits `{ source: 'keyboard' | 'mouse' }`.
- `SimulatedInputDriver` (same file, pure TS): programmatic `emit(source)`;
  used by ALL tests and by `npm run smoke`. Tests never import uiohook-napi
  (enforced by F12's AC).
- Global hook path (uiohook-napi, `src/main/globalInput.ts`): PRODUCTION ONLY,
  main process only, behind `systemPreferences.isTrustedAccessibilityClient(true)`
  called once at startup (never call with `false` first — electron#28395
  suppresses the prompt), lazy `require` inside try/catch (a broken native
  module must never crash startup), `uIOhook.stop()` on `will-quit`.
- Automatic graceful fallback to window-focused input (renderer `keydown` /
  `mousedown`, drag strip excluded) whenever the permission is missing or the
  hook fails; fallback listeners detach when global mode activates (F14).
- Real-hook behavior is verified ONLY in the Manual Verification Appendix (M4).
- Injected clock: no `Date.now`/`performance.now`/timers in `src/core` or
  `src/server` logic. Engine time advances only through `engine.tick(dt)`
  (injected dt; the renderer feeds rAF dt clamped to 100 ms): fever windows,
  companion volleys and cooldowns are measured on that clock (Assumption 39).
  The server takes `now()`, `randomUUID()`, `randomBytesHex()` and
  `randomSeed()` injected via `createApp(deps)` (PvP cooldown, rate-limit
  window, ids, seeds); production wires `Date.now` and `node:crypto` in
  `src/server/index.ts` only. `net.ts` takes `fetchFn` injected. Tests
  advance time explicitly; wall-clock time is never observed.
- Injected RNG (`mulberry32(seed)`; `resolvePvp` draws exactly twice; the
  boss capture draw follows the loot draw), injected store (`MemoryStore`)
  and injected `fetch` for the net client — tests never open sockets, never
  reach the network, never touch a real DB. `SMOKE=1` forces the client
  offline by code and isolates `userData` (Assumption 40).

## Non-Goals

- No auto-update mechanism.
- No Windows or Linux builds executed in this run — the electron-builder
  `win`/`nsis` section is config-only (F26); `npm run package` targets macOS
  arm64 only. No code signing or notarization.
- No localization; all text is English.
- No CI pipeline setup in this run.
- Networking exists ONLY in `src/main/net.ts` (client: injected fetch,
  `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, never throws, offline by default) and
  `src/server/**` (the Render server), offline-first: renderers and the menu
  never touch the network, tests never touch the external network, `SMOKE=1`
  forces offline. No telemetry, analytics or cloud saves (the leaderboard
  snapshot is name + score + roster only).
- No realtime or synchronous PvP; no PvP arena replay (banner + companion
  pop-in / scatter only); no match history or `matches` table.
- No accounts beyond nickname + bearer token: no passwords, e-mail, PII,
  nickname uniqueness, moderation or token rotation.
- No anti-cheat (accept-and-rank): leaderboard/PvP stats are self-reported;
  "server-authoritative" covers the PvP verdict and roster bookkeeping only;
  only shape/caps, rate limit, body cap and cooldown bound abuse.
- No paid Render tier, no DB rotation automation (manual runbook in
  `## Deployment`), no CORS (Electron main is the only client).
- No settings UI beyond the tray menu and the Collection & Battle window
  (no preferences window, no volume/mute control, no window-size or scale
  options, no hotkey to open the menu).
- No sound beyond the 4 synthesized WebAudio blips (Assumption 13).
- No balance tuning beyond the stated formulas; no equipment/abilities/trinket
  effects, no idle or offline progression, no achievements, no win/end state
  (rebirth is the only prestige).
- No multi-window features beyond the single overlay + the single menu
  window; single fixed-size overlay.

You are the Planner of the Desktop Monster harness. You decompose the v2 SPEC
delta into one-iteration task units and APPEND them to the existing

directly, and you edit it on the orchestrator's behalf.

2. `SPEC.md` (amended) — every new task must trace to F28+, `## Server / API`,

   `.harness/<HV>/reference/SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10 (resolve `<HV>` from
   `.harness/CURRENT`) — the suggested T22+ decomposition, already cut into
   4 parallel chains. Use it as your baseline; adjust as SPEC.md requires.
5. `.harness/<HV>/templates/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.template.md` — its header
   comment is the NORMATIVE grammar (plan-format v2).

   you. For every task run `graphify affected "<primary symbol or file>" --depth 2`
   and put its file hits into `Files:` and the tasks that produce those files
   into `Deps:`. `graphify query "<question>"` for orientation.
7. `.harness/<HV>/reference/TOOLING.md` §3 (codex sandbox limits) and §6
   (Render commands used by the deploy task).

- T01–T21 blocks and Iteration Log rows 01–21 are IMMUTABLE: never renumber,
  reorder, delete, or edit them (T21's `Deps: T01–T19` range stays — it is `[x]`).
- Replace the header comment at the top of the file, in place, with the
  template's v2 header (`plan-format: v2`).
- Continue numbering at T22. The FIRST new task is the server scaffold — its
  title contains the word `server`.
- Iteration Log: leave the v1 table untouched. Directly below its last row add
  a blank line and the v2 table header + separator
  (`| iter | ts | worker | task | result | gates | commit | note |`) as the
  LAST table in the file — `plan.mjs log-row` appends there. Nothing follows it.

Every task has `- Worker: claude` or `- Worker: codex` (the line after `Deps:`).
`codex` iff EVERY `Files:` path (ignoring `SPEC.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`,
`.agentdoc/**`) is in the graphics set: `src/renderer/sprites/**`,
`src/renderer/anim.ts`, `src/renderer/hud.ts`, `src/renderer/effects.ts`,
`static/style.css`, `static/menu.css`, `tests/sprites.test.ts`,
`tests/anim.test.ts`, `tests/effects.test.ts`, `tests/renderer.test.ts`,
`tests/window.test.ts`. One path outside the set → `claude`. The orchestrator
never re-decides; it routes by this field. Keep codex tasks few and coarse
(~5): font A–Z + symbols / effect presets + per-species hits / boss + companion
art / fever + PvP-result art / menu CSS + species canvas — each sandbox
round-trip is expensive.

- `Deps:` — `none` or comma-separated T-IDs only (`T22, T24`). No ranges, no
  prose. Backward only: Tn may depend only on T<n. Unknown tokens make a task
  unschedulable forever.
- `Files:` — COMPLETE: every file the task creates or edits, INCLUDING test
  files, `SPEC.md` when the task edits it, `package.json` + `package-lock.json`
  when dependencies change, `AGENTS.md` when it changes. One plain path per
  entry, comma-separated; no `{a,b}` groups, no `(new)` suffix (say "new" in
  Notes). Files overlap drives lane scheduling: `plan.mjs ready` withholds a
  task while any `[~]` task shares a path. A missing path = merge conflict
  later; an over-broad list = an idle lane.

  ACs use `npx vitest run <file>`, `grep`, `test -e`, `node -e`,
  `npm run build`, `npm run smoke`. Loopback `127.0.0.1` checks (`curl
  http://127.0.0.1:…/healthz`) are allowed in a builder AC ONLY for the
  server-scaffold boot proof (T22 / F43). External hostnames, `render` and
  `npm install` appear ONLY in the deploy tasks (T44 / T51), whose network
  part must be guarded so it passes hermetically:
  `[ -n "$DESMON_SKIP_NET" ] || curl -fsS --retry 5 --retry-delay 30 "$SERVER_URL/healthz"`.

  (no smoke / start / electron / network). codex tasks add no dependencies.
- `Notes:` — SPEC refs (F-ids — the loop injects those rows into the prompt),
  the exact formulas/literals/test titles to pin, the v1 tests the task must
  keep green (`tests/ipc.test.ts` IPC table `toEqual` + `registerIpcHandlers()`
  literal; `tests/tray.test.ts` menu order; `tests/renderer.test.ts` preload
  method regex; `GLYPH_CHARS` append-only; `tests/packaging.test.ts`
  `dist/**/*`), and dead-end warnings. `push: yes` appears ONLY in the deploy
  task's Notes, together with the exact push command (`git push origin HEAD:main`)
  and the `render-bootstrap.sh` + `render deploys create <srv-id> --wait --confirm`
  steps. A task that adds a dependency names the ponytail rung that failed in
  Notes; pre-approved: `pg@8.23.0` as a devDependency with a hand-written
  `src/server/pg.d.ts` (never `@types/pg`). No other new dependency without
  that line.

A task must be completable by ONE fresh-context agent in ONE iteration:
- touches ≤ 5 files (excluding the plan file and session records),
- ≤ ~300 changed LOC,
- exactly ONE gate-verifiable outcome.

the bigint conversion (T25 as specified in GAME_DESIGN_V2.md §13:
`formulas`/`types`/`engine`/`hud` + their tests; `loot.ts` untouched — a
half-converted core cannot typecheck). If in doubt, split. 24–32 new tasks total.

Cut the work into 4 independent chains with disjoint `Files:` sets and
cross-chain `Deps:` only at integration points:

  + `engine.tick`, fever, `collection.ts` lifecycle, `resolvePvp` (shared core);
- server chain — scaffold (`src/server/{index,http,app,store,pgStore,pg.d}.ts`,
  `tests/server*.test.ts`), players/snapshot/leaderboard, pvp + cooldown +
  rate limit, `PgStore`, deploy;

  menu CSS;
- menu/net chain — `src/main/{identity,net}.ts` (persistence.ts injection
  pattern), IPC additions, `static/menu.html` + `src/menu/{index,view}.ts`
  (`tsconfig.renderer.json` `include` += `src/menu`), tray item. Overlay
  banners and audio blip 4 belong to the core/renderer chain (T31 / T47).
Shared hotspots (`src/main/index.ts`, `src/shared/ipc.ts`, `src/preload/index.ts`,
`src/renderer/global.d.ts`, `tests/ipc.test.ts`, `src/renderer/game.ts`,
`package.json`) block lanes whenever two tasks list them: serialize such tasks
through `Deps:` instead of letting Files overlap idle a lane, and give each
integration task one chain's worth of wiring, not all of it.
Before finishing run `node .harness/<HV>/loop/plan.mjs ready` — it must print
at least 3 READY ids (server scaffold, bigint conversion, font A–Z), and the
longest Deps chain should be ≤ 14 tasks.

- T22 per SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md §10 (no pg, no MemoryStore, no
  tsconfig.test.json change; includes SMOKE isolation: `src/main/index.ts` and
  `tests/window.test.ts` in Files, `desmon-smoke-` userData tmpdir set BEFORE
  `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` when `process.env.SMOKE` is set, AC
  `&& grep -q "desmon-smoke-" src/main/index.ts`). Does NOT run

# AGENTS.md — Desktop Monster (DesMon)

This file is the heart of the loop: the single source of truth for how to build,
test, run, and package this project, and for what must pass before any work is

## What this project is

DesMon is a BongoCat-style desktop companion game: a small transparent always-on-top
pixel-art overlay where every keystroke/mouse click makes a knight attack a monster
(HP bar, kills, item drops, auto-collect, XP, levels). v2 adds bosses captured as
companions (auto-attack; consume / fuse / reincarnate / sacrifice / rebirth), fever mode,
A–Z big-number damage, per-species effects, a Collection & Battle window, and a small Node
server (`src/server`, on Render) for the leaderboard and asynchronous PvP with companion
stealing. Electron + TypeScript; all art is sprites-as-code (no binary assets). Built
autonomously by the parallel Ralph loop in `.harness/` — see `.harness/<version>/HARNESS.md`
(version in `.harness/CURRENT`).

## Commands (the contract)

bump (see HARNESS.md §Versioning).

## Code style — ponytail (lazy senior dev)

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code
never written. Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse it.
3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
Rules: no abstractions that weren't explicitly requested; no new dependency if it can be avoided;
no boilerplate nobody asked for; deletion over addition, boring over clever, fewest files possible;
shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem; question complex requests;
pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size; mark deliberate
corners with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling.

15	## Summary
16	
17	DesMon is a BongoCat-style macOS desktop companion: a small transparent,
18	frameless, always-on-top pixel-art overlay in which every keystroke or mouse
19	click makes a sword-wielding pixel knight attack a monster. Monsters have HP
20	bars; killed monsters scatter into pixels, drop items that are auto-collected,
21	grant XP, and are replaced by a stronger monster, while the hero levels up.
22	v2 (0.2.0) adds: every 8th monster is a boss that can be captured into a
23	30-companion roster that attacks alongside the hero; fever mode; a companion
24	lifecycle (consume / fuse / reincarnate / sacrifice / rebirth); unbounded
25	A–Z-suffixed damage numbers on native `bigint`; a Collection & Battle window;
26	and a leaderboard + asynchronous PvP with companion stealing against a small
27	Node server (`src/server`, Render free tier) — offline-first, the game never
28	waits on the network. Built with Electron + TypeScript, all art and sound
29	generated from code committed in-repo, verified end-to-end by the frozen
30	AGENTS.md command contract (`npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`,
31	`npm run smoke`, `npm run package`, `npm run start:server`).
32	
33	## Assumptions
34	
35	1. Hero stands on the LEFT facing right; monster on the RIGHT facing left — the requirement allows either side; fixing one makes rendering and tests deterministic.
36	2. Attack triggers are every `keydown` (OS auto-repeat included) and every `mousedown`, each counting as exactly one attack; key-up, mouse-up, scroll and mouse-move do not — matches the BongoCat per-event feel and is the simplest countable rule.
37	3. Progression formulas are frozen to GAME_ARCHITECTURE §2 as amended by GAME_DESIGN_V2 §1: `damageForLevel(l)=l`; crit chance 10% × multiplier 2; `monsterMaxHp(i)=⌊10·115^i/100^i⌋` computed as an exact `bigint` (`(10n*115n**i)/100n**i`, equal to the v1 double `⌊10·1.15^i⌋` for every i < 199); `xpReward(i)=5+3i`; `xpToNext(l)=⌊20·1.4^(l−1)⌋`; coins per kill `1+⌊i/3⌋`; trinket chance 25%; hero damage = `level × (crit ? 2 : 1) × (fever ? 3 : 1) × (1 + souls)` — exact formulas make every AC numerically decidable.
38	4. Exactly 5 monster species (slime, bat, ghost, golem, dragon) cycle forever, with a palette tint per `tier = ⌊index/5⌋`; every 8th monster (`index % 8 === 7`: 7, 15, 23 …) is a boss with 5× HP, 5× XP, 5× coins, a ` BOSS` name suffix and `MonsterDef.boss = true`, drawn at 3× with a crown — 8 is not a multiple of 5 so bosses cycle all species; bounds art effort while making endless scaling visible.
39	5. Progression is endless: no win state, no final boss. Rebirth at `monsterIndex ≥ 40` is a soft prestige: `souls += ⌊index/8⌋`, `rebirths + 1`, run resets to level 1 / monster 0 while companions, items, coins, kills, bestIndex and nextCompanionId are kept — DesMon stays a companion toy; souls multiply damage by `(1 + souls)`.
40	6. Trinket items are collection-only counters (5 kinds, weighted) with zero gameplay effect — keeps the engine minimal; coins and trinkets are just HUD/save counters.
41	7. The save file is `app.getPath('userData')/save.json` (`app.setName('DesMon')` so dev and packaged share it), schema `SaveFileV2` (bigint fields as decimal strings); `parseSave` migrates v1 saves and junk per field (independent fallbacks to `DEFAULT_SAVE`) and never throws — the app must never fail to boot because of a bad save; `serializeSave`/`createEngine` accept `SaveFileV1 | SaveFileV2`.
42	8. Damage is applied at input time; animations are presentation-only and never gate game logic — keeps the engine deterministic and key-mash-safe.
43	9. Animation timing state machines (hero IDLE/ATTACK; monster SPAWNING/IDLE/HIT/DYING) are pure functions in `src/core/fsm.ts`, advanced by injected `dt`, consumed by the renderer — the only way animation timing is unit-testable without a DOM.
44	10. The window is fixed at 320×220 CSS px (internal canvas 160×110, `image-rendering: pixelated`), not resizable, and draggable by mouse-dragging ANYWHERE on the overlay via a custom threshold drag (cursor deltas streamed to main over `desmon:move-window`; a press only becomes a drag after ~4px of cursor travel, so clicks remain attacks and the fallback path keeps receiving `mousedown`) — a full-window `-webkit-app-region: drag` would swallow the fallback clicks, so the CSS drag region stays limited to the legacy 24-px top strip. The default window position is the bottom-right corner of the primary display's work area (which already excludes the macOS Dock / Windows taskbar) inset by a 16px margin.
45	11. In SMOKE mode the app never touches uiohook, drives a `SimulatedInputDriver` to fire ≥3 synthetic attacks, and prints `SMOKE_OK` only after the renderer reports its first painted frame over IPC — smoke then proves boot + render + input path with zero permissions and zero interaction; under `SMOKE=1` the client is offline by code, `userData` is a fresh temp dir (Assumption 40) and the menu window is never created.
46	12. All UI text is English only — localization is a Non-Goal.
47	13. Sound is exactly 4 synthesized WebAudio blips (attack tick, kill arpeggio, level-up fanfare, fever start — an ascending 4-note square sweep), created lazily on first input, with no mute/volume UI — included only because it is trivially achievable without assets.
48	14. Dependency versions are pinned EXACTLY per GAME_ARCHITECTURE §0.2 (electron 39.8.10, eslint 9.39.4, typescript 5.9.3, typescript-eslint 8.63.0, vitest 3.2.7, vite 6.4.3, electron-builder 26.15.3, @types/node 22.20.0, uiohook-napi 1.5.5, no `^` ranges) plus v2's single pre-approved addition `pg` 8.23.0 in devDependencies only (ponytail rung 5: no stdlib Postgres client) — host Node 20.12.2 is the binding constraint; newer majors break install.
49	15. Statistical ACs use a fixed seed and tolerance bands (crit 8–12%, trinket 23–27%, PvP 1:3 power → 22–28% win rate, over 10,000 trials) — deterministic because the RNG is injected mulberry32.
50	16. The tray menu is the settings surface: title row, input-mode status / "Grant Accessibility…" item, separator, `Collection & Battle…` (opens the 380×520 framed DOM window `static/menu.html` with Roster / Ranking / Battle tabs; the tray item is its ONLY opener; never opened under `SMOKE=1`), `Reset Progress`, `Quit` — no other settings UI exists.
51	17. Hero and monster sprites render at `SPRITE_SCALE = 2` (each art pixel is a 2×2 canvas rect: hero 28×24, monsters 24×20 on the 160×110 canvas), and the `LV n` + XP gauge floats centered above the hero's head instead of the top-left corner — user-requested presentation change (2026-07-08); items, damage-number glyphs and HUD counters stay 1×. Bosses render at `BOSS_SCALE = 3` (36×30, HP bar raised to `BOSS_HP_BAR_Y = 54`); companions render at scale 1 in a column left of the hero (`COMPANION_X = 2`, slot gap 14, up to 3 active).
52	18. Numbers: monster HP, damage and companion power are native `bigint` (unbounded); coins/xp/level/kills/souls/rebirths/indices stay JS numbers because their curves are linear/logarithmic and cannot approach 2^53 in practice; JSON (save, IPC, wire) never carries a raw bigint — bigint fields travel as decimal strings.
53	19. `monsterMaxHp` is the exact rational floor `10·115^i/100^i`; it equals the v1 double formula for every index < 199, so v1 exact-value tests keep their values (type edits only, no test deleted; index 5000 has 305 digits).
54	20. Damage/power text uses truncating A–Z notation (`src/core/bignum.ts`): < 1000 verbatim; else 3 significant digits truncated (never rounded) + bijective-base-26 suffix by thousands-group (A = 10^3 … Z = 10^78, AA = 10^81, ZZ = 10^2106, AAA = 10^2109): 1000 → `1.00A`, 12345 → `12.3A`, 123456 → `123A`, 999999 → `999A`, 1e6 → `1.00B`, 1e9 → `1.00C`; `.` and every letter exist in the 3×5 font; coin/kill counters stay plain `String(number)`.
55	21. Save schema v2 stores bigint fields as decimal strings (`monsterHp ≥ '1'`); v1 saves migrate field by field (`bestIndex = monsterIndex`, `companions = []`, `nextCompanionId = 1`); junk never prevents boot; `createEngine` and `serializeSave` accept v1 or v2; `nextCompanionId` is raised above every existing `cN` id so re-minting never collides.
56	22. Every 8th monster (`index % 8 === 7`) is a boss: 5× HP, 5× XP, 5× coins, ` BOSS` name, drawn 3× with a crown; bosses cycle all five species; `loot.ts` is untouched (the engine multiplies the coin amount).
57	23. Boss kills capture the boss as a companion with probability 0.35 via ONE extra rng draw taken AFTER the loot roll and always consumed (so non-boss seeded event logs stay byte-identical to v1); companions are `{ id 'cN', speciesId, bossIndex, level 1..10, stars ≥ 0 }` with ids minted from `nextCompanionId` (never uuid); the roster holds at most `ROSTER_CAP = 30` — captures and PvP steals into a full roster are void (the draw is still spent).
58	24. Companion power = `max(1, ⌊monsterMaxHp(bossIndex)/20⌋) · level · 2^stars` (bigint); the 3 strongest (tie → lower numeric id) each hit once per 1000 ms of engine time (`COMPANION_ATTACK_MS`), never crit, ×3 during fever; their kills chain into the next monster inside the same volley, drop loot and can capture; no companions → no events and no rng draws.
59	25. Fever starts when 20 inputs land within 3000 ms of ENGINE time (advanced only by `engine.tick(dt)`; the renderer feeds rAF dt clamped to 100 ms), lasts 5000 ms, triples all damage, then a 10000 ms cooldown blocks re-trigger; never persisted (`toSave()` has no fever field); `feverStart` may precede the `attack` event of the triggering input; a throttled window can over-trigger — deterministic and accepted.
60	26. Lifecycle ops are pure and total (`applyCollection(state, action) → { state, events } | { error }`, never mutating input): consume (target.level += 1 + food.stars, cap 10, food removed, target ≠ food), fuse (same species + same stars → stars + 1, level 1, bossIndex = max, second removed), reincarnate (level 10 → level 1, stars + 1), sacrifice (removed, souls += 1 + stars), rebirth (Assumption 5), addCompanion (full → error), removeCompanions (unknown ids ignored), pvpResult (lost removed, stolen re-minted via addCompanion, dropped silently when full); only `rebirth` and `pvpResult` emit events; there is no `rosterChanged` action or event — the renderer flushes the save after every `apply`.
61	27. Hero damage = `level × (crit 2) × (fever 3) × (1 + souls)`; hero level is a minor stat — growth comes from companions and souls; balance beyond these formulas is a Non-Goal.
62	28. 37	## 1. Unbounded numbers — `src/core/bignum.ts`
38	
39	**Representation: native `bigint`.** Scope:
40	
41	| field | type | why |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| `GameState.monsterHp`, `MonsterDef.maxHp` | `bigint` | 10·1.15^i is exponential |
44	| `attack.damage`, `monsterHit.hpAfter`/`maxHp`, `companionAttack.damage` | `bigint` | subtracted from HP |
45	| `companionPower()`, `resolvePvp` powers | `bigint` | derived from `maxHp` |
46	| `level, xp, killCount, coins, monsterIndex, souls, rebirths, stars, bestIndex, nextCompanionId` | `number` | linear/log curves; never near 2^53 |
47	| save/wire copies of bigint fields | decimal `string` | JSON has no bigint |
48	
49	**Formulas (`src/core/formulas.ts`)** — exactly one line changes:
50	
51	```ts
52	export const monsterMaxHp = (index: number): bigint => {
53	  const i = BigInt(Math.max(0, Math.floor(index)));
54	  return (10n * 115n ** i) / 100n ** i; // exact floor(10·1.15^i); equals the v1 double for every i < 199
55	};
56	// damageForLevel, xpReward, xpToNext, CRIT_CHANCE, CRIT_MULT unchanged (number)
57	```
58	
59	Verified: equals `Math.floor(10 * 1.15 ** i)` for all i ≤ 198 (first divergence
60	i = 199, off by one — invisible to v1 tests which pin 0/5/10/20 and monotonic
61	0..49). Index 5000 → 305 digits in < 1 ms.
62	
63	**API**
64	
65	```ts
66	export function suffix(g: number): string;              // bijective base-26: 1→A … 26→Z, 27→AA, 52→AZ, 53→BA, 702→ZZ, 703→AAA; g ≤ 0 → ''
67	export function format(n: bigint | number): string;     // rule below; negative/non-finite number → '0'
68	export function ratio(num: bigint, den: bigint): number; // den ≤ 0n → 0; else Number(num * 10000n / den) / 10000 clamped to [0, 1]
69	export function bigField(raw: unknown): string | null;   // finite number → String(Math.max(0, Math.floor(n))); /^\d+$/ string → itself; else null (bigint input → null: not a JSON value)
70	```
71	
72	**Format rule (exact):** `s = n.toString()`. If `s.length ≤ 3` → `s`. Else
73	`d = s.length`, `g = ⌊(d − 1) / 3⌋`, `lead = d − 3g ∈ {1, 2, 3}`, `m = s.slice(0, 3)`;
74	text = (`lead === 3` ? `m` : `m.slice(0, lead) + '.' + m.slice(lead)`) + `suffix(g)`.
75	Truncation, never rounding.
76	
77	| n | text |
78	|---|---|
79	| 999 | `999` |
80	| 1000 | `1.00A` |
81	| 12345 | `12.3A` |
82	| 123456 | `123A` |
83	| 999999 | `999A` |
84	| 1e6 | `1.00B` |
85	| 1e9 | `1.00C` |
86	| 1e78 | `1.00Z` |
87	| 1e81 | `1.00AA` |
88	| 1e2106 | `1.00ZZ` |
89	| 1e2109 | `1.00AAA` |

257	## 6. Lifecycle — `src/core/collection.ts` (pure, total) and PvP resolution
258	
259	```ts
260	export const REBIRTH_MIN_INDEX = 40;
261	export type CollectionAction =
262	  | { type: 'consume'; targetId: string; foodId: string }   // target.level += 1 + food.stars (cap 10); food removed; target ≠ food
263	  | { type: 'fuse'; aId: string; bId: string }               // same speciesId && same stars: a.stars + 1, level 1, bossIndex = max(a, b); b removed
264	  | { type: 'reincarnate'; id: string }                      // level === 10 → level 1, stars + 1
265	  | { type: 'sacrifice'; id: string }                        // companion removed; souls += 1 + stars
266	  | { type: 'rebirth' }                                      // monster.index ≥ 40: souls += ⌊monster.index / 8⌋, rebirths + 1; level 1, xp 0, monster = monsterForIndex(0), monsterHp = maxHp(0); keeps companions/items/coins/killCount/bestIndex/nextCompanionId
267	  | { type: 'addCompanion'; companion: Companion }           // roster < ROSTER_CAP: pushed with id re-minted as `c${nextCompanionId++}`; full → error
268	  | { type: 'removeCompanions'; ids: string[] }              // unknown ids ignored; never an error
269	  | { type: 'pvpResult'; won: boolean; stolen: Companion | null; lostId: string | null }; // lostId removed (if present); stolen added via the addCompanion rule (dropped silently when full)
270	export function applyCollection(state: Readonly<GameState>, a: CollectionAction):
271	  { state: GameState; events: GameEvent[] } | { error: string };   // never mutates input; unknown type/ids → error
272	```
273	
274	Events: `rebirth { souls }` for `rebirth`, `pvpResolved { won, stolen, lostId }`
275	for `pvpResult` (`stolen` carries the re-minted companion or null); every other
276	action returns `events: []`. There is **no** `rosterChanged` action or event —
277	the renderer flushes the save after every `apply`.
278	
279	`engine.apply(a): GameEvent[]` — runs `applyCollection` on the live state;
280	`{ error }` → returns `[]`, state untouched. Fever state is preserved across
281	apply. `bestIndex` is untouched by rebirth.
282	
283	**PvP resolution (shared with the server, T32):**
284	
285	```ts
286	export function resolvePvp(attacker: readonly Companion[], defender: readonly Companion[], rng: Rng):
287	  { attackerWon: boolean; moved: Companion | null; attackerPower: bigint; defenderPower: bigint };
288	```
289	
290	Rule: `attackerPower = Σ companionPower(attacker)`, same for defender;
291	`p = total === 0n ? 0.5 : ratio(attackerPower, total)`; draw 1: `attackerWon = rng.next() < p`;
292	loser = the other roster; draw 2 is ALWAYS consumed: `victim = loser[⌊rng.next() · loser.length⌋]`
293	(null when the loser is empty); `moved = victim` unless the winner's roster
294	already holds `ROSTER_CAP` companions (then null). Exactly 2 rng draws per call.
295	Bot ("Training Dummy") and cooldown rules are the server's (`SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md`);
296	the server calls `resolvePvp(attackerRoster, defenderRoster, mulberry32(seed))`
297	and moves `moved` between stored rosters. The client applies the outcome via
298	`pvpResult`.

15	## 0. Decisions at a glance
16	
17	| Topic | Decision |
18	|---|---|
19	| Runtime | `node:http` + `pg` only. No framework, no `@types/pg`, no separate tsconfig. |
20	| Location / build | `src/server/**` compiled by the EXISTING `tsconfig.main.json` → `dist/electron/server/index.js`; excluded from the .app by electron-builder. |
21	| Auth | `POST /v1/players {nickname}` → `{playerId, token}`; server stores `sha256(token)`; bearer on every other `/v1` call. |
22	| Identity storage | `userData/identity.json`, main-process only. NOT in `save.json`; the token never crosses IPC. |
23	| Score | `bestIndex DESC, rebirths DESC` — plain integers. No BigNum keys on the wire or in SQL. |
24	| PvP | Async, server-resolved: opponent = rank neighbour (`seed & 1` → up/down) or bot "Training Dummy"; verdict = shared core `resolvePvp(attacker, defender, mulberry32(seed))`; steal one uniformly random companion (none if loser empty, winner full, or bot). |
25	| Anti-cheat | **Accept-and-rank**, stated openly: snapshots are self-reported; "server-authoritative" means the verdict + roster bookkeeping only, never stat integrity. |
26	| Abuse bounds | 60 req/min per key, 64 KB body cap, 60 s PvP cooldown, one snapshot row per player, shape/caps validation. |
27	| Storage | One `players` table (jsonb snapshot + integer score columns). No matches table, no history. |
28	| Tests | `createApp().handle()` + `MemoryStore`, injected `now/randomUUID/randomBytesHex/randomSeed`; the http adapter is tested with injected streams. No sockets in `npm test`; network only in T44/T51 ACs behind `DESMON_SKIP_NET`. |
29	| Deploy | Render free tier via CLI (`loop/render-bootstrap.sh`, idempotent by name); explicit `render deploys create --wait`; `/healthz` returns the built sha for verification. |

130	## 3. HTTP API (`/v1`, JSON, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`)
131	
132	Error body is always `{ "error": "<code>" }` plus `retryAfterSec` on 429. Codes:
133	
134	| Status | `error` | When |
135	|---|---|---|
136	| 400 | `bad_request` | malformed JSON, wrong shape, invalid nickname/snapshot, bad `name` on register |
137	| 400 | `no_snapshot` | `POST /v1/pvp` before any successful `PUT /v1/snapshot` |
138	| 401 | `unauthorized` | bearer missing/unknown on a bearer-required route, or present-but-unknown on `/v1/leaderboard` |
139	| 404 | `not_found` | unknown method/path |
140	| 413 | `payload_too_large` | body > 65 536 bytes (adapter; request destroyed) |
141	| 429 | `rate_limited` | > 60 requests per fixed 60 s window for the key |
142	| 429 | `cooldown` | `POST /v1/pvp` within 60 s of the caller's last PvP |
143	| 500 | `internal` | store threw; `handle()` never throws |
144	
145	| Method / path | Auth | Request | Response |
146	|---|---|---|---|
147	| `GET /healthz` | – | – | 200 `{"ok":true,"sha":"<RENDER_GIT_COMMIT or dev>"}` — answered by http.ts, never touches the store |
148	| `POST /v1/players` | – | `{ "nickname": string }` | 201 `RegisterResponse` |
149	| `PUT /v1/snapshot` | bearer | `Snapshot` | 200 `SnapshotResponse` |
150	| `GET /v1/leaderboard?n=10` | bearer optional | – | 200 `LeaderboardResponse` (`me` null without bearer or before the first upload) |
151	| `POST /v1/pvp` | bearer | body ignored (`{}`) | 200 `PvpResponse` |
152	
153	Rules:
154	- **Auth**: `token = randomBytesHex(16)` (32 hex chars, injected), stored as `sha256(token)` hex
155	  (`node:crypto` `createHash('sha256')`); `playerId = randomUUID()` (injected). Nicknames are not unique.
156	- **Score / rank**: order by `(bestIndex DESC, rebirths DESC)`. `rank = 1 + count(players with a snapshot whose
157	  (bestIndex, rebirths) > mine)` — ties share a rank. Players without a snapshot are invisible to rank/top/neighbour.
158	- **Upload**: validate → strip every companion whose id is in the caller's `stolenIds` → store snapshot (name
159	  column := `snapshot.name`, `updated_at := now`) → return `{ rank, removed: strippedIds }`. `stolenIds` is kept
160	  (last 32; stripping is idempotent) — the loser learns here, on whichever upload comes first.
161	- **Leaderboard**: `n` = integer query param clamped to `1..LEADERBOARD_MAX`, default `LEADERBOARD_DEFAULT`;
162	  `top` = first n rows in score order with ranks computed by the tie rule; `me` = the caller's row or null.
163	- **Neighbour pick** (`POST /v1/pvp`): `seed = randomSeed() >>> 0` (injected). `up = store.neighbor(me.id, key, 'up')`
164	  = nearest player with score strictly greater; `down = store.neighbor(me.id, key, 'down')` = nearest with score
165	  ≤ mine, excluding me (equal scores count as "down"). Both exist → `seed & 1 ? down : up`; one exists → that one;
166	  none → **bot** `{ name: 'Training Dummy', bestIndex: me.bestIndex, rebirths: me.rebirths, companions: [] }`
167	  with `bot: true`. The bot never steals and is never stolen from; a bot match mutates only `lastPvpAt`.
168	- **Verdict**: `resolvePvp(me.snapshot.companions, opponent.companions, mulberry32(seed))` from
169	  src/core/collection.ts (§5). `win = verdict.attackerWon`.
170	- **Steal bookkeeping** (non-bot only; see §5 for the exact steps): move `verdict.moved` from loser to winner,
171	  re-id'd to `'s' + seed`; `setStolenIds(loser, [...loser.stolenIds, verdict.moved.id].slice(-32))` using the loser's
172	  ORIGINAL id; `putSnapshot` both rows; `setLastPvpAt(me.id, now())`. `verdict.moved` is null when the loser's roster is
173	  empty or the winner's stored roster already has `ROSTER_CAP` companions ("full roster wins nothing").
174	  Two non-transactional row updates — a concurrent match against the same loser could double-steal; accepted
175	  corner (single free instance + per-player cooldown), marked with a `ponytail:` comment naming `BEGIN/COMMIT` as the upgrade.
176	- **Cooldown**: `PVP_COOLDOWN_MS = 60_000` per caller via `lastPvpAt`; inside the window → 429 `cooldown`,
177	  `retryAfterSec = ceil((PVP_COOLDOWN_MS - elapsed) / 1000)`. `now()` is injected (never `Date.now()` in app.ts).
178	- **Rate limit**: fixed 60 s window, `RATE_LIMIT = 60` per key; key = `sha256(bearer)` when a bearer is present,
179	  else `ip:<ApiRequest.ip>`; `ApiRequest.ip` = first entry of `x-forwarded-for` (trimmed), falling back to
180	  `socket.remoteAddress` (Render fronts the service with a proxy — the socket address is the proxy). In-memory
181	  `Map`, pruned lazily when it exceeds 10 000 keys; resets on restart. 429 `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSec`.
182	- **Body cap**: `BODY_LIMIT = 65_536` bytes, enforced in http.ts by counting chunks; on overflow respond 413 and
183	  `req.destroy()`. Empty body → `body: null`.
184	- **No PII**: nickname only; the ip is a transient rate-limit key and is never stored or logged. No CORS
185	  headers (the only client is Electron main's `fetch`).
186	- **Accept-and-rank**: only shape/caps are validated. No plausibility bounds on `bestIndex`/`rebirths`/rosters —
187	  a clicker has no server-verifiable proof of play. Stated in README and handoff (§8).
188

294	## 5. PvP resolution
295	
296	Shared core contract (src/core/collection.ts, T32 — full definition and `companionPower`/roster power in
297	GAME_DESIGN_V2.md; restated here because the server depends on it byte-for-byte):
298	
299	```ts
300	export function resolvePvp(attacker: readonly Companion[], defender: readonly Companion[], rng: Rng):
301	  { attackerWon: boolean; moved: Companion | null; attackerPower: bigint; defenderPower: bigint };
302	```
303	- Pure, deterministic, exactly **two** `rng.next()` draws in this order: (1) win roll —
304	  `attackerWon = rng.next() < p` with `p = attackerPower / (attackerPower + defenderPower)` (roster powers per
305	  GAME_DESIGN_V2 §6; both zero → 0.5); (2) steal index — `Math.floor(rng.next() * loser.length)`, drawn even when
306	  no steal applies so sequences stay stable.
307	- `moved` = the loser's companion at that index, or null when the loser's roster is empty or the winner's roster
308	  length ≥ `ROSTER_CAP`. `attackerPower`/`defenderPower` are returned for the client's presentation only — the
309	  server never puts them on the wire (§2 `PvpResponse`). Core knows nothing about bots.
310	- Server and client (VICTORY/DEFEAT presentation, T36) never re-run the maths; the response carries the outcome.
311	
312	Server steps for `POST /v1/pvp` (after auth, rate limit, cooldown check):
313	1. `me = getByToken(...)`; `me.snapshot` null → 400 `no_snapshot`. `setLastPvpAt(me.id, now())` (even for bots).
314	2. `seed = randomSeed() >>> 0`; pick the opponent (§3 neighbour rule) or the bot.
315	3. `verdict = resolvePvp(me.snapshot.companions, opponent.companions, mulberry32(seed))`; `win = verdict.attackerWon`.
316	4. Bot → respond `{ bot: true, seed, win, opponent: bot, stolen: null, lost: null }`; no store writes beyond step 1.
317	5. Non-bot, `verdict.moved === null` → respond with `stolen: null, lost: null`; no roster writes.
318	6. Non-bot steal: `loser/winner` = by `win`; `transferred = { ...verdict.moved, id: 's' + seed }` (companion ids are
319	   unique per player only — `c<N>` counters — so a transferred companion gets a server id that cannot collide);
320	   `loser.snapshot.companions = without(verdict.moved.id)`; `winner.snapshot.companions.push(transferred)`;
321	   `setStolenIds(loser.id, [...loser.stolenIds, verdict.moved.id].slice(-STOLEN_IDS_MAX))`; `putSnapshot(loser)`,
322	   `putSnapshot(winner)`. Respond `stolen: win ? transferred : null`, `lost: win ? null : verdict.moved`.
323	7. The attacker applies `stolen`/`lost` immediately (client, §6). The **defender** learns on its next
324	   `PUT /v1/snapshot`: the server strips ids in `stolenIds` and returns them as `removed`; the client removes them.

459	## 8. Known limitations (copy into handoff.md §Deployment / §Known limitations)
460	
461	- **Accept-and-rank**: leaderboard and PvP inputs are self-reported; "server-authoritative" covers the verdict and
462	  roster bookkeeping only. A one-line client edit wins every match. Bounded by rate limit, body cap, cooldown.
463	- Free web service sleeps after 15 min idle; cold start ≈ 1 min exceeds `NET_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) — the first
464	  leaderboard/PvP click after a long idle may fail with `network`; opening the menu warms the dyno; retry works.
465	  750 h/month cap.
466	- Free Postgres expires 30 days after creation (14-day grace), no backups: identities and the board are
467	  disposable; rotation is manual (§7). Expiry date recorded in AGENTS.md §Server / meta.json `db_expires`.
468	- Single instance: in-memory rate limiter resets on restart; steal is two non-transactional row updates.
469	- Defenders learn about a stolen companion only on their next upload (§5 step 7); until then the local roster
470	  keeps a ghost companion that still attacks locally but is absent from the server snapshot.
471	- Background uploads ignore `removed`; the correction arrives on the next menu-driven sync.
472	- Bot matches ("Training Dummy") never steal either way; a player alone on the board can only fight the bot.
473	- Probe accounts (`probe-*`, bestIndex 0) accumulate at the bottom of the board, one per network AC run.
474	- No nickname uniqueness, no moderation, no token rotation, no CORS (Electron main is the only client).

239	  boss capture draw follows the loot draw), injected store (`MemoryStore`)

788	## 14. Pre-resolved assumptions (SPEC §Assumptions, numbered after v1's 17)
789	
790	18. Numbers: monster HP, damage and companion power are native `bigint` (unbounded); coins/xp/level/kills/souls/rebirths/indices stay JS numbers because their curves are linear/logarithmic and cannot approach 2^53 in practice.
791	19. `monsterMaxHp` is the exact rational floor `10·115^i/100^i`; it equals the v1 double formula for every index < 199, so v1 exact-value tests keep their values (type edits only, no test deleted).
792	20. Damage/power text uses truncating A–Z notation: < 1000 plain; else 3 significant digits + bijective-base-26 suffix (A = 10^3 … Z = 10^78, AA = 10^81, ZZ = 10^2106, AAA …); `.` and every letter exist in the 3×5 font.
793	21. Save schema v2 stores bigint fields as decimal strings; v1 saves migrate field by field; junk never prevents boot; `createEngine` and `serializeSave` accept v1 or v2.
794	22. Every 8th monster (`index % 8 === 7`) is a boss: 5× HP, 5× XP, 5× coins, ` BOSS` name, drawn 3× with a crown; bosses cycle all five species.
795	23. Boss kills capture the boss as a companion with probability 0.35 (one rng draw after loot, always consumed); companions are `{ id 'cN', speciesId, bossIndex, level 1..10, stars }`; the roster holds at most 30 — captures and PvP steals into a full roster are void.
796	24. Companion power = `max(1, ⌊maxHp(bossIndex)/20⌋) · level · 2^stars`; the 3 strongest (tie → lower id) hit once per 1000 ms of engine time, never crit, ×3 during fever; their kills chain, drop loot and can capture.
797	25. Fever starts when 20 inputs land within 3000 ms of ENGINE time (advanced only by rAF dt), lasts 5000 ms, triples all damage, then 10000 ms cooldown; never persisted; a throttled window can over-trigger — deterministic and accepted.
798	26. Lifecycle ops are pure and total: consume (+1 + food.stars levels, cap 10), fuse (same species + stars → stars + 1, level 1), reincarnate (level 10 → level 1, stars + 1), sacrifice (→ souls += 1 + stars), rebirth (index ≥ 40 → souls += ⌊index/8⌋; resets level/xp/monster; keeps roster, items, coins, kills, bestIndex).
799	27. Hero damage = `level × (crit 2) × (fever 3) × (1 + souls)`; hero level is a minor stat — growth comes from companions and souls; balance beyond these formulas is a Non-Goal.
800	28. Effects are data presets over the existing 200-slot particle pool, deterministic (index-derived angles, no rng); each species, the hero (cyan; gold with souls), companions (projectile), bosses (shockwave), captures (sparkle) and fever (aura) have distinct presets.
801	29. Collection/Ranking/Battle UI is a second 380×520 framed DOM window (`static/menu.html`) opened only from the tray; the game window owns the engine; main relays actions and the last written save to every other window; no hotkey; never opened under SMOKE.
802	30. Sound is four synthesized blips (v1 three + fever start).
803	31. Identity is `userData/identity.json` `{ playerId, token, name }` held by main only; credentials are server-issued on first sync; default name `Knight-xxxx`; display name ≤ 16 chars; 401 → re-register; cheating via save edits is not defended beyond server shape caps.
804	32. All networking lives in main (`src/main/net.ts`, Node fetch, 5000 ms timeout, offline-first: `NetResult` errors, game unaffected); renderers never touch the network; `SMOKE=1` and an empty `SERVER_URL` force offline by code; sync is inline at three moments (after a changed save write, before leaderboard, before PvP) — no scheduler.
805	33. Leaderboard score = deepest monster index reached (`bestIndex`) desc, ties by `rebirths` desc; stats are self-reported (accept-and-rank).
806	34. PvP is asynchronous and server-simulated with core `resolvePvp` (win chance = my power / total over full rosters; the loser loses one uniformly random companion to the winner unless the winner is full; bot "Training Dummy" never steals); the server picks the opponent (rank neighbour by `seed & 1`); 60 s cooldown; the menu forwards the outcome to the game as a `pvpResult` action; no arena replay.
807	35. Server is a Node 20.12.2 `node:http` + `pg` service in `src/server`, compiled by `tsconfig.main.json`, deployed to Render free tier from GitHub main via `render-bootstrap.sh`; free Postgres expires after 30 days (documented, recreatable); `/healthz` never touches the DB.
808	36. The bigint cutover is one atomic 7-file task; `it(` counts per test file never decrease; pinned lists are extended, never shrunk.
809	37. Package version becomes 0.2.0 (tray title, README artifact names, packaging test, F25 literal follow).
810	38. Codex workers own only the graphics file set (sprites/**, anim/hud/effects.ts, CSS, their tests); they never run Electron, git or the network; every `game.ts`/menu hook-up is a claude task; the orchestrator runs smoke.

name: desmon-2-dev
description: Stage 2 of the Desktop Monster harness (v2) — the parallel-lane Ralph loop. Runs `iterate.sh loop` in the background; it dispatches up to LANES ready tasks into git worktrees (a fresh `claude -p` builder or `codex exec` graphics worker per task), merges each finished lane into main, re-runs gates (+ smoke when needed) and is the plan file's single writer. The orchestrator only waits, services re-plan requests and (fallback) in-session claude lanes, then hands off to desmon-3-eval on ANY exit code. Requires SPEC.md and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (run desmon-1-plan first).
---

# desmon-2-dev — Parallel Ralph loop stage (v2)

You are the ORCHESTRATOR. You never implement game code, never run gates or
smoke by hand (`collect` did — its logs are the evidence), never edit
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (`plan.mjs` inside the loop is its single writer),
never merge, never push. Every worker is a fresh process/subagent in its own
worktree; the repo files are the only shared state.

## Setup

`HV=$(cat .harness/CURRENT)`; `TS=$(cat .agentdoc/LATEST)`; `S=.agentdoc/$TS`.
Abort with a clear message if SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md or `$S/meta.json`
is missing, or `meta.json.harness_version` ≠ `$HV` (one session ↔ one
version: run desmon-1-plan first).
`MAX_ITER` = user value or 50; `LANES` = user value or 3; pass `CLAUDE_MODEL`,
`CODEX_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_TIMEOUT`, `CODEX_TIMEOUT` only if the user set them.
`NESTED_CLAUDE` = the `NESTED_CLAUDE=` line in `$S/sessions/stage1-plan.md`
(else `.harness/$HV/reference/TOOLING.md §7`; else probe now, with the same
nine-variable `env -u` list `iterate.sh` uses:
`env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION -u CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_PID -u CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET -u CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN -u CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA claude -p 'Reply with exactly PROBE_OK' --output-format text`).
`git worktree list` must show no `lane/` worktrees left by a crashed run;
if it does, follow HARNESS.md §5 first (collect, or remove + `set-status ' '`
+ `rm -f $S/lanes/<id>.*` so no stale `.iter` occupies a lane). A lane whose
worker pid is gone without an `.rc` is self-healed by `iterate.sh` (treated as
rc 999 → CRASHED at the next `status`/`dispatch`/`loop` pass).

## A. Primary path (NESTED_CLAUDE=1)

1. Start the loop via the Bash tool with `run_in_background: true`:
   ```
   RUNNER=in-session NESTED_CLAUDE=1 LANES=$LANES MAX_ITER=$MAX_ITER \
     bash .harness/$HV/loop/iterate.sh loop; echo "LOOP_EXIT=$?"
   ```
   (add the model/timeout vars on the same line if set). It repeats
   `dispatch` → sleep 15 → `collect <id>` for every lane whose `.rc` exists,
   until converged, capped, blocked, crashed or deadlocked; every collect
   commits plan + logs and appends a row to `$S/sessions/dev-loop.md`.
2. WAIT for the completion notification. Never `sleep`-poll in the
   foreground. `bash .harness/$HV/loop/iterate.sh status` is the only
   progress probe (read-only); use it at most once per notification.
3. RE-PLAN requests (BLOCKED ×2 on a task) are serviced by the loop itself on
   this path: `collect` archives `$S/prompts/12x-replanner-iter-NN.md`
   (`agents/10-planner.md` + "re-scope ONLY task <id>"), the loop runs
   `claude -p` with it, commits `docs(plan): re-scope <id> [ralph]` and
   removes `$S/lanes/REPLAN-<id>`. You do nothing; the re-planner is the
   ONLY agent besides `plan.mjs` that edits IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, and only
   that task's block/children.
4. On completion read `LOOP_EXIT` and `$S/sessions/dev-loop.md`
   (`| iter | worker | task | result | gates | smoke | commit | decision |`).

## B. Fallback path (NESTED_CLAUDE=0) — you drive the same contract

`dispatch` will not spawn claude lanes; it prints
`PENDING <id> <prompt-path> <lane-dir>` for each (codex lanes are spawned
normally and are unaffected). Run the loop body yourself:
1. Foreground: `RUNNER=in-session NESTED_CLAUDE=0 LANES=$LANES bash .harness/$HV/loop/iterate.sh dispatch`;
   parse the `PENDING` lines.
2. For EVERY PENDING line, in ONE message, spawn a fresh general-purpose
   subagent whose prompt is the exact contents of `<prompt-path>` (dispatch
   already appended the rendered `INSESSION_NOTE.md` to it — it tells the
   subagent its working directory is `<lane-dir>` and to end with the status
   JSON on the first line; do NOT append the note again). No other context.
   When it returns: write its final message verbatim to
   `$S/sessions/iter-NN.log` (NN = `cat $S/lanes/<id>.iter`), then
   `echo 0 > $S/lanes/<id>.rc` (the Agent tool has no exit code; a missing or
   unparseable JSON is what `collect` grades as CRASHED).
3. Codex lanes: wait for `$S/lanes/<id>.rc` with a background Bash
   `until [ -f "$S/lanes/<id>.rc" ]; do sleep 15; done`
   (`run_in_background: true`, wait for its notification).
4. For each lane whose `.rc` exists:
   `bash .harness/$HV/loop/iterate.sh collect <id>` (foreground; it merges,
   verifies, records, cleans up). Read its `DECISION=`: `escalate-crash` →
   drain running lanes, then stop as exit 3; `escalate-blocked` → the task is
   now `[!]` (informational; exit 2 comes from step 6 when nothing else is
   dispatchable). A `$S/lanes/REPLAN-<id>` file (content = path of the
   archived re-planner prompt) → spawn a fresh general-purpose subagent with
   that prompt's exact contents, wait for it, commit
   `git add IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md $S && git commit -m "docs(plan): re-scope <id> [ralph]"`
   (the re-planner writes its record to `$S/sessions/replan-<id>.md` and does
   not commit), then `rm "$S/lanes/REPLAN-<id>"` BEFORE the next `dispatch`
   — the re-scope happens before the retry, never after it.
5. Repeat from 1 while `cat $S/sessions/.iter` < `MAX_ITER`; at the cap stop
   dispatching, drain running lanes (3–4), then treat the outcome as exit 1.
6. When `dispatch` prints an empty `READY=` and `status` lists no lanes, run
   `RUNNER=in-session NESTED_CLAUDE=0 bash .harness/$HV/loop/iterate.sh verdict`
   ONCE in the foreground — the final verdict only, no dispatch: no open
   tasks → gates + smoke on main → exit 0 (converged; exit 4 if red);
   otherwise exit 2 if any `[!]` task remains, exit 1 at the iteration cap,
   exit 4 (deadlock) otherwise. That exit code is `LOOP_EXIT`. (`iterate.sh
   loop` refuses `NESTED_CLAUDE=0` with exit 64 — never call it on this path.)

## Exit

Exit codes: 0 converged (no open tasks; gates + smoke green on main) ·
1 iteration cap (`MAX_ITER` dispatched) · 2 blocked escalation (BLOCKED ×3 on
one task) · 3 crash escalation (CRASHED ×3 on one task) · 4 deadlock (nothing
ready, no lanes, open tasks remain — e.g. only `[!]` left).
- Append below the table in `$S/sessions/dev-loop.md`:
  `outcome: exit <N> (<meaning>), iterations <n>, lanes <LANES>, nested_claude <0|1>`.
- `git worktree list` must show no `lane/` worktrees (kept branches
  `lane/<id>-crash-N` / `-conflict-N` / `-red-N` are evidence — leave them).
- `git add -A .agentdoc && git commit -m "docs(agentdoc): stage-2 dev loop exit <N> [harness $HV]"`.
- Report exit code + meaning, iterations used, tasks done/split/blocked, and
  proceed to desmon-3-eval on ANY exit code — it writes the handoff
  (INCOMPLETE when needed). Never leave the session without stage 3 running.

# AGENTS.md — Desktop Monster (DesMon)

This file is the heart of the loop: the single source of truth for how to build,
test, run, and package this project, and for what must pass before any work is
declared done. Every agent (human or AI) reads this first.

## What this project is

DesMon is a BongoCat-style desktop companion game: a small transparent always-on-top
pixel-art overlay where every keystroke/mouse click makes a knight attack a monster
(HP bar, kills, item drops, auto-collect, XP, levels). v2 adds bosses captured as
companions (auto-attack; consume / fuse / reincarnate / sacrifice / rebirth), fever mode,
A–Z big-number damage, per-species effects, a Collection & Battle window, and a small Node
server (`src/server`, on Render) for the leaderboard and asynchronous PvP with companion
stealing. Electron + TypeScript; all art is sprites-as-code (no binary assets). Built
autonomously by the parallel Ralph loop in `.harness/` — see `.harness/<version>/HARNESS.md`
(version in `.harness/CURRENT`).

## Commands (the contract)

These script names are FROZEN. Changing any of them requires a harness version
bump (see HARNESS.md §Versioning).

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | install dependencies (lockfile is committed) |
| `npm start` | build then launch the app (Electron) |
| `npm test` | unit tests (Vitest; deterministic — no network, no real timers, no real OS input hooks) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, zero warnings allowed (`--max-warnings 0`) |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` over all tsconfig projects, strict |
| `npm run smoke` | build, launch Electron with `SMOKE=1`; the app prints `SMOKE_OK` to stdout after the window loads and exits 0 by itself (non-zero exit or 20s watchdog timeout = failure). Must run headful on macOS without user interaction |
| `npm run package` | unsigned macOS build via electron-builder (`CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`); output under `release/` |
| `npm run start:server` | `node dist/electron/server/index.js` — leaderboard/PvP server (Render start command; reads `PORT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `RENDER_GIT_COMMIT`). Created by the loop's server-scaffold task T22; `src/server` compiles via `tsconfig.main.json`'s include, so `typecheck` covers it unchanged |

## Server

SERVER_URL=<set by the deploy task>
- `GET /healthz` → `200 {"ok":true,"sha":"<RENDER_GIT_COMMIT|dev>"}`, no DB access; everything
  else under `/v1` (SPEC.md §Server / API).
- Deploy = `git push origin main` + `render deploys create <srv-id> --wait --confirm` (webhooks
  not guaranteed). Provisioning = `.harness/<CURRENT>/loop/render-bootstrap.sh` (idempotent),
  run only by the loop's deploy task, which also fills the placeholder above.
- Free tier: web service sleeps after 15 min idle (~1 min cold start — the client must tolerate
  it and work offline); Postgres 1 per workspace, 1 GB, EXPIRES 30 days after creation (`db_expires`).
- The server is authoritative for the PvP verdict and roster moves only; leaderboard stats are
  self-reported (accept-and-rank).

## Verification gates (the exit condition)

The gates line, verbatim — run it exactly like this:

    npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck

Rules:
- No task may be checked off in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` unless this line exits 0.
- No commit is "done" while gates are red.
- The loop may not declare convergence unless this line exits 0 (plus `npm run smoke`) on `main`
  AND the plan file has no open tasks.

## Definition of done (loop level)

ALL of the following:
1. Every task in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` is `[x]` or `[s]` (no `[ ]`, `[~]`, `[!]`).
2. The gates line exits 0.
3. `npm run smoke` exits 0.
4. `npm run package` produces `release/` containing the DesMon .app and .dmg.
5. Every `AC:` in `SPEC.md`'s feature table passes when executed literally.
6. Deploy verification passed (`/healthz` ok with the deployed sha) — or `DESMON_SKIP_NET` recorded in the handoff.

## Workers

Every task carries `- Worker: claude | codex`. The orchestrator (`.harness/<CURRENT>/loop/iterate.sh`)
dispatches up to `LANES` tasks in parallel, each in its own git worktree `.worktrees/<id>` (branch
`lane/<id>`), and merges finished lanes into `main` itself. Codex = graphics only (sprites/anim/hud/
effects/css + their tests) in a sandbox with no network, no Electron, no git; Claude = everything else.
- Work ONLY inside your worktree; never `git push`, `git checkout main`, `git worktree`, `git merge`, `git rebase`.
  Exception: a task whose Notes contain `push: yes` runs exactly `git push origin HEAD:main` once, after its
  commit and gates.
- Never edit `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` or `SPEC.md` (unless SPEC.md is in the task's Files); report
  through the final status JSON (`task, result, gates, commit, note[, children]`) on the FIRST line
  of your final message.
- Exactly ONE task per iteration; read this file, the task block + SPEC rows in your prompt, and
  only the source you need (`graphify query`/`affected` first — `graphify-out/` is symlinked into your
  worktree by dispatch, read-only; run `graphify update .` in the lane only if missing). Do not read the whole plan.
- Run the gates line and the task's `AC:` before DONE; errors → a different approach; BLOCKED only
  for environmental impossibility after ≥3 attempts (evidence in `note`).
- Session record → `<session dir>/sessions/iter-NN.md` inside the worktree.
- Claude commits inside the worktree; Codex never commits and never runs `npm start|smoke|package`,
  `electron`, `npm install`, and adds no dependencies.
- SPLIT = implement nothing, return `children[]`, leave the tree clean.
Charters: `.harness/<CURRENT>/agents/20-builder.md`, `25-gfx-worker.md`; loop contract: `HARNESS.md §4`.

## Code style — ponytail (lazy senior dev)

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code
never written. Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse it.
3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
Rules: no abstractions that weren't explicitly requested; no new dependency if it can be avoided;
no boilerplate nobody asked for; deletion over addition, boring over clever, fewest files possible;
shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem; question complex requests;
pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size; mark deliberate
corners with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling.
Not lazy about: understanding the problem, input validation at trust boundaries (IPC payloads,
`parseSave`, the HTTP server, the net client), error handling that prevents data loss, security,
accessibility, real-hardware calibration, anything explicitly requested. Non-trivial logic leaves
ONE runnable check — here that means a vitest test (installed dependency, rung 5). Full ruleset +
review/audit format: `.harness/<CURRENT>/reference/PONYTAIL.md` (MIT, DietrichGebert/ponytail).

## Observability

- `rgt log --oneline -n 20`, `rgt blame <file>[:line]`, `rgt sessions` — agent activity history
  (hooks in `.claude/settings.json` / `.codex/config.toml`).
- `graphify query "<question>"`, `graphify affected "<symbol>" --depth 2` — code-graph orientation;
  `graphify update .` refreshes it.
- Exports: `.agentdoc/<TS>/sessions/iter-NN.rgt.json`, `.agentdoc/<TS>/graph/`. `.regent/` and
  `graphify-out/` are local caches (gitignored); `.worktrees/` = live lanes.

## Hard rules

- NEVER delete, skip (`.skip`/`xit`), weaken, or comment out a test to make gates pass.
- NEVER lower tsconfig or ESLint strictness, and never add `|| true`-style shims.
- NEVER report a task DONE without executing its `AC:` command in the same iteration and seeing it pass.
- One task per iteration. Keep changes scoped to the dispatched task.
- Tests must be deterministic: injected RNG (seeded), injected input driver (`SimulatedInputDriver`),
  injected clock; no external network (loopback-free: server tests use injected streams/stores),
  no real DB; no reliance on real global hooks or wall-clock time.
- No new dependency without a Notes line naming the ponytail rung that failed (pre-approved: `pg`).
- Workers never edit `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` and never work outside their worktree. Codex commits
  are made by the orchestrator with a `[codex]` suffix.

## Commit convention

`<type>(T<NN>): imperative subject` — e.g. `feat(T03): knight attack animation state machine`.
Orchestrator: `docs(agentdoc): dispatch|collect iter NN <id> … [ralph]`, `docs(plan): re-scope <id> [ralph]`,
`chore(wip): auto-commit stray changes before <dispatch|collect NN> [ralph]` (real uncommitted changes on main
outside `.agentdoc/`/`.worktrees/` — live lane output is never auto-committed); codex lanes:
`<type>(T<NN>): <title> [codex]`.

## macOS environment notes

- Global input capture (uiohook-napi) requires the Accessibility permission, which CANNOT be
  granted programmatically — and uiohook crashes the process if started without it. Automated
  tests and `npm run smoke` MUST use the simulated input driver. Real global hooks are verified
  manually only (see SPEC.md §Manual Verification Appendix).
